(b) The statement class reaches the main RPC statement through PostgREST hoisting of function settings, applied transaction-scoped before the main query, on a shared client. This covers function-RPC routes only, not direct DML or writer trigger paths outside the 17. (c) The lock class can be separated within function scope through proconfig. With the profile's ceilings and the 8000ms gate headroom, any single route value refuses at least one class: T<=5000 makes every writer, including prepublication platform writes, refuse at the gate; 5000<T<=20000 refuses intake. findings.title: Documented server-side original-clock readers make the gate headroom and elapsed-transaction checks authorable in-slice
findings.claim: STEWARD.md:170 and QOE-03 say no original-deadline reader exists and imply that excluded scope is needed. PostgreSQL documents statement_timestamp() (receipt of the latest client command message, i.e. the top-level statement), transaction_timestamp()/now() (transaction start) and clock_timestamp(). Nested statements, savepoints and exception blocks cannot reset them. The 8000ms remaining-statement and remaining-transaction check before the exclusive gate, and the commit's elapsed-transaction check, can be written in the in-slice SQL. Caveats: (1) in extended protocol the statement timer starts at the first Parse/Bind/Describe while statement_timestamp() marks the latest message, so the remaining time can be slightly overestimated; (2) the deadline basis is a configured value, not proof of an armed timer; (3) if the transaction timer was armed after BEGIN, using transaction_timestamp() is conservative.

findings.title: Function-scope semantics: guard proconfig misses triggering-row waits; plain SET leaks; effective timer ordering

That wait is governed by the writer route's timers, not the guard's 7000ms proconfig (reasoned, NOT RUN). (2) A plain SET (without LOCAL) inside any body persists past function exit and, if committed, on the pooled PostgREST connection. (3) PG ignores the longer of statement/idle when transaction_timeout is <= it, so effective values must keep strict idle < statement < transaction ordering for each class. The writer relation list states only statement < transaction (PROFILE.json:304).
findings.evidence: CREATE FUNCTION doc: SET clause applied 'when the function is entered'; plain SET 'persist[s] after function exit, unless the current transaction is rolled back'. - Function proconfig must equal exactly search_path="".

LOGIN ROLE (session_user): UNKNOWN. Not inferred to be 'authenticator' or service_role.

REQUEST ROLE: service_role by source intent only (SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY). The actual JWT-to-role mapping, memberships and role settings are UNKNOWN. No readback under SECURITY DEFINER is named yet; that is carried at S2.

DEFINER OWNER O: the requirement is defined (equal to the provider-fence owner, with rolsuper or rolbypassrls; intake.sql:341-345). The actual OID is UNKNOWN. The owner-only admin login route is UNKNOWN. Under SET ROLE O, O's own role settings do not load.

CLIENT/HTTP TIMEOUT: ABSENT at S0. Any later deadline only stops the caller waiting. After possible transmission the outcome is OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN with the original key. A client abort is not rollback.

GATEWAY: UNKNOWN. Lens K reports a 60 s maximum from the Supabase timeouts page; I did not re-fetch it.

POOL ACQUISITION 1000 ms: proposed only. The steward maps it to PostgREST's seconds-valued db-pool-acquisition-timeout, which is instance-wide. Not configured or observed.

DATABASE LIMITS (PostgreSQL 17 documentation as cited by the steward and lenses; NOT RUN):
- lock_timeout: applies to each lock acquisition (55P03) and is consulted at each wait, so a value validated at function entry governs the waits that follow inside that function.
- statement_timeout: runs from command arrival (extended protocol: from the first Parse, Bind, Execute or Describe until Execute or Sync completes) and expires with 57014. It cannot be re-armed in the middle of a statement.
- transaction_timeout: covers the whole transaction and terminates the session (25P04). Prepared transactions are excluded. Setting it inside an open transaction is undocumented, so it must be armed before BEGIN.
- idle_in_transaction_session_timeout: terminates the session (25P03).
- deadlock_timeout: a detector interval, settable only by a superuser or with SET privilege.
- If transaction_timeout is at or below statement or idle, the longer timer is ignored.

WHEN EACH TAKES EFFECT:
- Login-time database/role settings (precedence: database-role > role > database), postgresql.conf and startup options apply at connection start. They are shared by all traffic on that route.
- PostgREST applies impersonated-role settings and hoisted function settings transaction-scoped, after BEGIN and before the main query. This rests on the steward's citation only; docs.postgrest.org returned HTTP 429 to the lenses, so it is unverified.
- A function SET clause applies on entry and is restored on exit. A plain SET persists past function exit unless the transaction rolls back.
- In-SQL readback (current_setting, statement_timestamp, transaction_timestamp) proves consistency, never arming.

CONSEQUENCES:
- Statement expiry aborts the statement and leaves the transaction unable to commit.
- Transaction or idle expiry terminates the session.
- Neither proves when rollback or lock release completes. The 1000 ms cleanup allowance is unmeasured.
- Disconnect, caller deadline, gateway or body-less errors, 25P03/25P04 and any unconfirmed commit are OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN, with the same key and same-actor replay recovery.
- A false TRY and a confirmed-abort 55P03/40P01/40001 from a main-statement error body give DEFINITE_REFUSAL_RETRYABLE, mapped to the existing 503 with the same key.
- There is no automatic retry or reactivation.

CLASS SEPARATION: on today's single route, no single value set before BEGIN admits both intake (transaction at most 5000) and writers (at least 8000 remaining at the gate), so one class always refuses. That is fail-closed. Distinct routes, or a separately reviewed amendment, are an S4 prerequisite.

ORIGINAL CLOCKS: the start instants can be read in SQL, and transaction_timestamp() is the conservative one. The armed timer value cannot be proven in-slice.

(b) r3 MD259 requires the same source at S, qualification and installation, so compiled NONPRODUCTION values would become the installed values wherever the source is installed. That is a guessed production default, which GRANT_235:45 does not authorize.
